For each component, agents first create an Isabelle/HOL theory with a specification, a soundness proof, and a reference checker made by code generation, then a fast Rust implementation, verified with Verus against a specification that mirrors the Isabelle definitions line by line. Specifications are frozen after independent review and cannot be changed by the implementing agents. A trust manifest lists what is still trusted. We built trust chains for SAT (verified LRAT checking); SMT, with certificates from an extended z3 and verified bit-blasting for bit-vectors and floating point; answer-set programming, with native certificates from clingo, including weight rules and optimality; and, closing the loop, Verus's final verification-condition step, by translation validation. All 3,726 SMT queries from 20 crates are certified and validated, and 15,662 answer-set proofs are accepted by both the Isabelle and the Verus checker. We found soundness defects in three proof checkers, including drat-trim, and in five solvers, including clasp and z3, which report wrong unsatisfiability.

papers.title: On non-canonical maximum cliques in the block graphs of orthogonal arrays
papers.summary: In this note, we prove an Erdős-Ko-Rado characterisation of maximum intersecting families of columns of certain orthogonal arrays. This solves a problem of Chris Godsil and Karen Meagher and implies that, in all orthogonal arrays OA$(m,(m-1)^2)$, every non-canonical maximum intersecting family of columns necessarily has the structure of an affine plane.

papers.title: Quadratic unitary Cayley graphs over finite commutative rings
papers.summary: Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with identity, and let $T_R=Q_R\cup(-Q_R)$, where $Q_R=\{u^2:u\in R^\times\}$. In this paper, we investigate the spectral properties of quadratic unitary Cayley graphs $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$, over finite commutative rings with identity. We determine all the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ when $R$ has odd characteristic. Our results extend the previously known spectral formulas for this family of graphs. We also obtain all the eigenvalues when the characteristic of $R$ is $2$. Furthermore, for rings of odd characteristic, we give a complete characterization of when $\operatorname{Cay}(R,T_R)$ is a strongly regular Cayley graph.

papers.title: Note on polychromatic coloring of hereditary hypergraph families III
papers.summary: For every integer $h\ge4$ we construct a hereditary family of hypergraphs with $m_2=h$ and \[ m_3\ge 2(h-1)+2\left\lfloor\frac{h-1}{3}\right\rfloor+1 \approx \frac{8}{3}m_2. \] This improves the lower bound $m_3\ge 2m_2$ from the preceding notes for every $m_2\ge4$. We also show that the worst-case integrality gap of the weighted transversal problem over hereditary families with $m_2\le h$ is between $h-1$ and $5000h$. As a consequence, every such family admits strong $\varepsilon$-nets of size at most $5000h/\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Cayley Regression for Finite Groups with a Cyclic Subgroup of Index Two
papers.summary: A finite group $G$ is a Cayley regression if every generalized Cayley graph of $G$ is isomorphic to a Cayley graph of $G$, and a $k$-Cayley regression if this holds for all such graphs of valency at most $k$. We show that the dihedral group $D_{2n}$, $n\geq2$, is a $2$-Cayley regression if and only if it is a $3$-Cayley regression, which holds exactly when $n$ is a prime power, and that for $k\geq4$ it is a $k$-Cayley regression if and only if $n$ is an odd prime power or $n\in\{2,4\}$. Groups with a cyclic subgroup of index two that are neither cyclic nor dihedral are not even $2$-Cayley regressions; consequently, a group with a cyclic subgroup of index two is a Cayley regression if and only if it is isomorphic to $C_2$, $C_4$, $C_6$, $C_{10}$, or $D_{2n}$ with $n$ as above. Finally, every split metacyclic group $C_m\rtimes C_q$ with $m>2$ and odd $q\geq3$ is not a $2$-Cayley regression.

papers.title: Rank-unimodality of one-descent composition ideals
papers.summary: The principal ideal of a composition consists of its distinct generalized subwords, ranked by the sum of their parts. We prove rank-unimodality for every composition with at most one descent and for every bitonic composition. Both the part sizes and the number of parts are unrestricted. The main ingredient is a coupling for a monotone host. If a subword is chosen uniformly among those of weight at most n, its length and its unused weight can be made to increase weakly when n increases by one. A decreasing threshold on the next available part then compares the positive difference of two ordinary rank coefficients with an earlier cumulative ratio. This supplies the coefficient inequality in the hereditary reduction at a strict peak.

papers.title: Rate--burst safety languages: the Farey structure of the burst boundary and discrimination under erasures
papers.summary: A leaky-bucket constraint with rate \(ρ\) and burst \(B\) allows at most \(ρn+B\) costly steps in every window of \(n\) consecutive steps. The infinite 0/1 words that satisfy it form a safety language. For a finite graph with edge costs 0 and 1, we study the least burst at which the cost word of some infinite path lies in this language, as a function of the real rate. This function is the exact tolerance of a monitor that distinguishes two finite-state systems observed through an erasure channel with a leaky-bucket bound. The language is \(ω\)-regular at every rational rate but not at irrational rates once the burst reaches 1, so ultimately periodic witnesses do not come from automata theory. We prove directly that simple lassos suffice at all real rates and that all breakpoints of the boundary lie in the Farey sequence of order N for a graph with N vertices. One lasso has a tight bound of order N to the power 2/3 on its affine pieces, whereas the choice among paths creates downward jumps and boundaries that are neither convex nor concave. One evaluation at the mediant of each Farey interval recovers the affine piece and an optimal lasso, and a greatest-fixed-point computation over decreasing integer bursts yields the whole function in polynomial time and linear working space. We also compute discrimination horizons and extend the Farey structure to turn-based safety games.

papers.title: Spectral radii of connected graphs with prescribed maximum degree
papers.summary:
For a real number $α>0$ and a positive integer $r$, we give recursive characterizations of the existence of finite simple connected graphs $G$ with adjacency spectral radius $ρ(G)=α$ and maximum degree $Δ(G)\le r$ (or $=r$). Adding one vertex to a graph $F$ at a time to update the Schur-complement $q=α-{\mathbf b}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}{\mathbf b}$, where $B=αI-A(F)$ is positive definite and ${\mathbf b}$ is a nonzero $0$--$1$ that specifies the neighbours of $z$ in $F$. Realizability is characterized by admissible constructions with positive intermediate outputs $q$ and a final zero output. We also establish a reduction for a graph $G$ obtained by attaching pairwise disjoint rooted trees, each by a single edge, to a nonempty connected graph $H$. Assume that $αI-A(T)\succ0$ for every attached tree $T$. For each $z\in V(H)$, let $q_{z,1},\ldots,q_{z,s_z}$ be the positive root pivots obtained by the scalar tree recursion for the trees attached to $z$, and set
  \[
  a_z=α-\sum_{j=1}^{s_z}q_{z,j}^{-1},
  \qquad
  M_H(\mathbf a)=\operatorname{diag}(a_z:z\in V(H))-A(H),
  \] where an empty sum is zero. Then $ρ(G)=α$ if and only if $M_H(\mathbf a)\succeq0$ and $\det M_H(\mathbf a)=0$. Taking $H=K_1$ recovers the tree criteria, while $δ(H)\geq2$ gives criteria for graphs with prescribed 2-core $H$. In particular, for unicyclic graphs of prescribed cycle length, path continuants reduce the spectral condition to positivity inequalities and one scalar equation.

papers.title: KAM theory for contact Hamiltonian systems
papers.summary: In both finite and infinite dimensions, we establish the first frequency-preserving KAM theorems for full-dimensional Legendrian tori in contact Hamiltonian families with general analytic coupling between the momenta and the contact variable. After adjustment of external parameters, the flow on each torus is analytically conjugate in the original time to the prescribed translation, with estimates uniform as the damping parameter crosses zero. This coupling can generate nonzero mean damping at first order even when the damping parameter vanishes. In finite dimensions, nonzero mean damping yields a time-preserving analytic contact linearization near the torus. In both settings the invariant graphs give global analytic solutions of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations whose characteristic flows are conjugate to the prescribed translation. A novel consequence in finite dimensions is that, under global Tonelli assumptions and strict increase in the contact variable, this analytic solution is both the unique forward and the unique backward weak KAM solution, and its associated Legendrian graph is an invariant torus carrying quasi-periodic dynamics.

papers.title: The Gerards-Schrijver conjecture on the Edmonds-Johnson property is false
papers.summary: An integral matrix $A$ has the Edmonds-Johnson property if, for all integral vectors $b,c,l,u$, the first Chvátal closure of $\{x: b\le Ax\le c,\ l\le x\le u\}$ equals its integer hull. Gerards and Schrijver conjectured that a totally half-modular matrix has the Edmonds-Johnson property if and only if it has no minor equal to one of two specific matrices, of size $3\times3$ and $3\times4$. We disprove this conjecture. We give a totally half-modular $5\times6$ matrix that does not have the Edmonds-Johnson property and has no minor equal to either matrix. It is a minimal obstruction: every proper minor has the Edmonds-Johnson property. The proofs work on a graph whose edges are the rows and bounds of the matrix, and on which the minor operations act by deleting, contracting and halving edges. For minimality, we reduce every proper minor to two classes of matrices known to have the Edmonds-Johnson property.

papers.title: The Schürmann-Vallentin lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering in dimension six
papers.summary: We prove that the lattice $\mathsf{L}_6^{c}$ discovered by Schürmann and Vallentin in 2006 is the unique (up to similarity) six-dimensional lattice that gives the thinnest lattice sphere covering.

papers.title: A $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-Approximation for Weighted 3-Set Packing
papers.summary: We give a deterministic $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-approximation for weighted $3$-set packing, for every fixed rational $\varepsilon>0$, improving on the 1.6908-approximation reported by Tong and Xu (2026). The algorithm has two phases. It first performs bounded local search using a rounded $12/7$-power potential. It then combines compatible exchanges that insert at most three sets and increase the original weight. The analysis relates the gap left by the first phase to the gain available to the second phase. We prove a structural inequality that bounds the weight of a comparison packing by $3/2$ times the current weight plus one sixth of a sum of small-exchange gains. Each gain accounts for all sets that the exchange must delete. A greedy rule recovers enough of these gains to obtain the approximation guarantee. We derive the structural bound from local optimality by analyzing finite computation trees and averaging the error caused by their limited depth. The running time is $n^{4^{O(1/\varepsilon)}}\operatorname{poly}(L)$, where $n$ is the number of input sets and $L$ is the input encoding length. The same guarantee holds for maximum-weight independent set in induced $K_{1,4}$-free graphs.

papers.title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
papers.summary:
Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[
  |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.

papers.title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
papers.summary: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describes the output shared by all trajectories up to the order $k^-$, which gives the moment a time-domain interpretation when the steady-state interpretation is not available. Finally, we show that the concept of moment matching also naturally extends as the definition of nonlinear moment is extended to an equivalence class. The ansatz also plays a crucial role in the extended notion of moment matching. The results are illustrated by a numerical example.

papers.title: From two heptagrams to a 449-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph
papers.summary: We construct a 5-chromatic unit-distance graph on 449 vertices. Previously, the smallest known 5-chromatic unit-distance graph had 509 vertices. Our graph is a subgraph of a graph obtained by a simple greedy construction applied to a 14-vertex seed graph consisting of two heptagrams.

papers.title: Bound to be Complete: Efficient Verification for SQL Equivalence via U-Expressions
papers.summary:
Automated verification of SQL query equivalence is a fundamental problem in database area. Recent works developed verifiers with guaranteed completeness, which can generate counterexamples to disprove non-equivalent queries and are useful in various scenarios. However, they have to solve complex formulas and can fail to produce counterexamples within a reasonable time budget.
  This paper presents a new complete verifier called SQLution, which not only greatly reduces the verification time, but also supports more SQL features. The key insight is to represent SQL semantics using U-expression, a functional algebra that can model SQL with significantly simpler formulas than prior works, thereby leading to more efficient SMT solving. To turn this insight into a practical verifier, SQLution further tackles two technical challenges associated with modeling SQL using U-expression, namely, the lack of tuple ordering and the presence of unbounded summations. In particular, to support tuple ordering, SQLution proposes order semantics encoding which combines U-expressions with first-order logic. To handle unbounded summation, SQLution introduces unbounded summation expansion to transform them into bounded summations, which can be directly encoded into FOL formulas. Evaluation shows that compared with state-of-the-art verifiers, SQLution can support all 271 non-equivalent query pairs derived from the Spider dataset and reduces verification time by up to 98.6%.

papers.title: Sharp $s$-nice recurrence without the van der Corput property
papers.summary:
For every real $s>2$, we construct a set $R_s\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ which is a set of $t$-nice measurable recurrence exactly for $t\ge s$ and is not a van der Corput set. The new ingredient of this construction is the Density Frankl--Rödl theorem. Furthermore, the probability measure $σ_s$ which witnesses failure of the van der Corput property has an atom at zero with mass $(s-2)/(2s-2)$. A Gaussian tail argument proves both sharpness of the recurrence exponent and the fact that this atom is the largest possible for any $s$-nice recurrent set. The result sharpens the recurrence separations of Bourgain and Mountakis, answers a question of Mountakis about the maximal mass of an atom at zero, and answers a question of Forrest about separating the various degrees of nice recurrence.
  In the appendix we give a self-contained proof of the Density Frankl-Rödl theorem.

papers.title: Kleinian groups generated by two elliptics of even order
papers.summary: Let $Γ<\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ be a non-elementary discrete group generated by two elliptics of even order, with a nontrivial relation in the corresponding free product of cyclic groups. We classify the possible compact orbifold cores of $\mathbb H^3/Γ$, together with their cusp data and marked meridians. They are finite meridional fillings of the two-bridge link and Heckoid models of Akiyoshi--Ohshika--Parker--Sakuma--Yoshida. Their weighted graphs have at most two standard tunnels, whose weights in the two-tunnel case are $2$ and an odd integer. The original generators are powers of primitive meridians which generate $Γ$, and we determine the possible meridian placements for all even orders. The groups are geometrically finite, their conformal boundary components are turnovers, and each oriented core with its cusp data determines its complete hyperbolic holonomy up to Möbius conjugacy. The proof uses trace rigidity, dihedral surgery, half-turn symmetries, and an index-two cover.

papers.title: Totally odd clique immersions in graphs with bounded independence number
papers.summary:
We prove that every $n$-vertex graph with at least one edge and independence number at most an integer $a\ge2$, where $n\ge a$, contains a totally odd strong immersion of \[
  K_{\left\lceil (n+a-1)/(2a-3/2) \right\rceil}, \] with every branch path of length at most $2a-1$. We also prove that every graph $G$ with independence number at most $a$ and no totally odd strong $K_t$-immersion with branch paths of length at most $2a-1$ satisfies \[
  χ(G)\le\left\lfloor \frac{(2a-3/2)(t-1)-a+2}{2} \right\rfloor \] where $t\ge2$. These bounds reduce the leading denominator coefficient in the general order bound from $9/4$ to $2$ and the colouring coefficient for independence number two from $3/2$ to $5/4$.

papers.title: Lattices of Minimal Covolume in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ over Dyadic Local Fields
papers.summary: In this paper, we determine the minimal covolume among lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ for each finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_2$. Using the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ on its Bruhat--Tits tree, we investigate the shape of the fixed subtrees of finite subgroups, particularly cyclic and dicyclic subgroups of $2$-power order. We determine which larger vertex stabilizers can occur at boundary vertices of the fixed subtrees of dicyclic subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $2.A_4$. We use these results to construct graphs of groups defining lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ and prove that these lattices attain the minimal covolume. This extends a result of Lubotzky and Weigel, which treats finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for odd primes $p$.

papers.title: Lean Census: A Distributional Analysis of AI-Generated Lean Code
papers.summary: We compare two human-written and four AI-generated Lean libraries with Mathlib through the distributions of simple statistics of their code. For each library we measure inline claims in proofs, proof length, how often each declaration is used, and design choices such as instances and private declarations, and we read each against the variation among Mathlib's own areas. The AI-generated libraries have more inline claims per theorem, longer proofs, fewer instances, and more private declarations than the human-written ones. We release the code for the analysis as a package, lean-census, at https://github.com/project-numina/lean-census.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28955v1.title: Z[tau]-フォーム：Goodman-Strauss の Dodecafoam の正二十面体加群における算術としての定式化
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28955v1.summary: Goodman-Strauss の Dodecafoam は、正十二面体を大きさ tau^{-k}（tau=(1+√5)/2）の十二面体の泡で埋める置換規則であり、星形化の12平面が切り分ける7種類のセルを用いる。本論文ではこれを階数3の Z[tau]-加群の厳密な算術として書き換える。この加群は6本の五回軸が張る M であり、正二十面体群が GL(3,Z[tau]) の120個の行列として作用する。膨張したセルの配置がセルの和集合になるための必要十分条件は、そのファセット水準が {±1, ±tau³} に属し、かつ十二面体内に収まることである。この有限線形系を全スケールについて同時に解くことで、幾何学的探索で知られていた22個の規則が正確に得られ、スケール 1, tau, tau², tau³ 以外には規則が存在しないことが示される。置換は6つ組上の整数演算となり、幾何学的フォームの泡を正確に再現する。M の点が大きさ tau^{-k} の泡の中心かどうかは、フォームを構築せずに高々 k+3 個の厳密な符号ベクトル（アドレス）で判定でき、同一サイズの全泡は、ガロア共役が |x*| ≤ 2 tau^k を満たす M の点をふるい分けることで得られる（この上界は計算機支援で証明される）。大きさ tau^{-k} の泡の個数は A beta^k + O(|beta'|^k)（beta=(1+√29)/2）で漸近し、泡中心の再スケールされた共役の閉包はボックス次元が高々 log_tau(beta)=2.4123<3 であるため、泡は内部を持ついかなる cut-and-project 窓でも選別されない。1999年の論文の他のフォームは本フォームの部分フォームである。規則リストが許す50400個の置換は18899個の泡集合を与え、Dodecafoam は試験した深さまででそのうち13440個の積集合である。4次元では、120-cell の星形カットに対する同じ線形系が幾何学的探索の718個のクラスタを再現し、スケール sqrt(5) tau² を追加する。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28955v1.appendix: 関連分野：aperiodic order and discrete patterns（置換タイリング、準結晶、cut-and-project）、combinatorics on words（置換規則・語の複雑性）、computer-assisted proofs（上界の計算機支援証明）。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28952v1.title: {-1,0,1} を成分とする冪零三重対角行列
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28952v1.summary: 成分が {-1,0,1} である冪零三重対角行列をすべて決定する。対角成分 d と相対する非対角成分の積 b_k の組 (d,b) の集合 𝒩ₙ を、特性多項式が λⁿ となる条件で特徴づける。𝒩ₙ は n の偶奇に応じた2種類の明示的な「折り畳み」操作により 𝒩⌊n/2⌋ から得られることを示す。その結果、𝒩ₙ が空でないのは n=1 または 3·2ʲ-1 ≤ n ≤ 2ʲ⁺²-1（ある j≥0）のときに限られ、その場合の要素数は 2^⌊log₂n⌋ である。これにより {-1,0,1} 成分の冪零 n×n 三重対角行列の個数の公式が得られ、その値は 1,9,73,585,4809,39113 で始まる。d=0 の場合は先行論文で証明された Corless の予想である。主要な新要素は剛性現象で、n≥2 の組の特性多項式が mod 4 で λⁿ に合同ならば、それはより小さい組の折り畳みでなければならない。したがって特性多項式が mod 2^{1+⌊log₂n⌋} で λⁿ に合同ならば冪零となる。最後に、Corless の歪対称族に属する m×m 行列の固有値 0 の重複度は高々 2^{v₂(m+1)}-1 で、等号が達成されることを示す。分類、剛性命題、集合 𝒩ₙ の濃度、および mod 2^{1+⌊log₂n⌋} の判定法は Lean 4 で形式化されている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28952v1.appendix: 関連分野: 列挙型組合せ論（冪零三重対角行列の計数）、計算機支援証明（Lean 4 による形式化）。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28888v1.title: 3つのほぼ対称なメタタイルがSpectreタイリングを生成する
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28888v1.summary: Spectre非周期モノタイルに対する3つのメタタイルからなる系「D23」を提案する。これはhatタイリングに対するHTPF系と同様の概念であり、メタタイル自身が置換系を持ち、任意回数反復した後、最下位のメタタイルをSpectreタイルに変換できる。3つのメタタイルのうち1つは2回回転対称性を持ち、残り2つはそれぞれ2次と3次の「ほぼ対称」である。すなわち、タイルのn回デフレーションが覆う領域はその回転と完全には一致しないが、それらの共通部分内で不一致タイルの割合はn→∞で0に収束する。この近似的対称性はSpectreタイリング自体の近似的対称性に対応する。この系の興味深い性質として、3つのメタタイルのうち1つはSpectreへの変換で完全に消滅する。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28888v1.appendix: 関連分野: aperiodic order and discrete patterns（非周期モノタイル・置換タイリング）。補足: 本論文は非周期モノタイルの置換構造と対称性の近似に関する研究であり、該当分野に直接関連する。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.title: エノン型自己同型写像に対する力学系マニン＝マンフォード予想
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.summary: 複素アフィン平面上の多項式自己同型写像で力学次数が1より大きいものに対し、DujardinとFavreが提唱した力学系マニン＝マンフォード予想を証明した。すなわち、既約代数曲線がそのような自己同型写像の周期点を無限個含むのは、その曲線が、自己同型写像のある反復をその逆写像に共役させる多項式インボリューションの固定軌跡である場合に限ることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28843v1.appendix: 関連分野: arithmetic dynamics（力学系マニン＝マンフォード予想は周期点の分布に関する予想であり、本論文は複素力学系の枠組みでこれを扱っている）。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28776v1.title: 非重複符号に関するBlackburn予想の証明
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28776v1.summary: 符号語の空でない真の接頭辞が他の符号語の接尾辞とならないような符号を非重複符号と呼ぶ。長さn、アルファベットサイズqの非重複符号の最大サイズSₙ(q)について、LevenshteinはSₙ(q) ≤ cₙqⁿ（ただしcₙ = (1/n)((n-1)/n)^(n-1)）を示した。アルファベットを分割するI, Jに対し符号I^(n-1)Jはnがqを割り切るときこの上界を達成し、Blackburnは任意のnと十分大きいqに対し最良のそのような符号が最大非重複符号であると予想した。本論文はこの予想を証明する。証明では極大非重複符号を記述する入れ子分割の生成関数を用いる。さらに、|I| = (n-1)q/nを満たす符号I^(n-1)Jとその反転のみがLevenshteinの上界を達成することを示す。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28776v1.appendix: 関連分野: combinatorics on words（符号理論・語の組合せ論）

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28606v1.title: レート・バースト安全言語：バースト境界のFarey構造と消失下での識別
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28606v1.summary: レートρとバーストBによるリーキーバケット制約は、任意の連続するnステップの窓において高コストのステップを高々ρn+B回まで許容する。この制約を満たす無限0/1語は安全言語を形成する。辺コストが0と1の有限グラフに対し、ある無限パスのコスト語がこの言語に属するような最小バーストを実レートの関数として研究する。この関数は、消失チャネルとリーキーバケット束縛を通して観測される2つの有限状態系を識別するモニタの正確な許容度を与える。言語はすべての有理レートでω正則であるが、バーストが1に達すると無理レートではω正則でなくなるため、最終周期的な証人はオートマトン理論からは得られない。すべての実レートで単純なlassoで十分であること、およびN頂点グラフに対して境界のすべてのブレークポイントが位数NのFarey列に属することを直接証明する。1つのlassoはそのアフィン片上でNの2/3乗オーダーのタイトな束縛を持つのに対し、パスの選択は下向きのジャンプと凸でも凹でもない境界を生み出す。各Farey区間の中間点での1回の評価でアフィン片と最適なlassoが回復され、減少する整数バースト上の最大不動点計算により多項式時間・線形作業空間で関数全体が得られる。さらに識別ホライズンを計算し、Farey構造を交代制安全ゲームへ拡張する。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28606v1.appendix: 関連分野：combinatorics on words（語上の制約・言語）、symbolic dynamics（有限型シフトに関連する有限グラフ上の経路とω正則言語）、computer-assisted proofs and validated numerics（多項式時間アルゴリズムと不動点計算）、equational theories of words and monoids（安全言語の構造）。
